name: Bánh su sê Cù Lao Chàm
nameVi: Bánh su sê Cù Lao Chàm
summary: Bánh su sê Cù Lao Chàm is a tapioca cake with shredded coconut and a mung-bean filling, tied in banana leaf. The Hội An World Heritage centre’s 25 November 2014 inventory gives the method. Its 7 July 2014 note names the cake and gives none. This is not the Da Nang cake molded in coconut leaf. No current price was printed.
origin: Cham Islands. A cake the 25 November 2014 inventory says had then been on Tân Hiệp for about 20 years, learned from the mainland.
texture: The inventory cooks tapioca starch with water and white sugar for about half an hour, then mixes in shredded mature coconut. The filling is mung bean, soaked, cooked, pounded, and cooked again with white sugar. Peanut oil goes on the hands. The packet is banana leaf tied with a banana-leaf string. The tie is how you tell it from bánh ít, which is not tied. It is then steamed in an aluminum pot. No minute count was printed.
howToEat: From the pier baskets, with bánh ít. The 25 November 2014 inventory says one household then made this cake, and that unsold cakes came back to the pier. It names no shop.
A current price is Check on arrival.
where: The pier, and Bai Lang, where the inventory places the baskets. No shop was named.
seoTitle: Bánh su sê Cù Lao Chàm — tied banana-leaf cake
seoDescription: Tapioca, coconut, and mung bean, tied in banana leaf, from the pier baskets on Tân Hiệp. A current price is Check on arrival.
